First, note that the series can be written as

$$
9{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n(n+1)}.
$$

Using partial fractions we can write the series as

$$
9{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+1}).
$$

Computing the first few partial sums, starting with $n=3,$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{3} & =9[(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4})] \\ {s}_{4} & =9[(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\frac{1}{5})] \\ {s}_{5} & =9[(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\frac{1}{6})] \\ {s}_{6} & =9[(\frac{1}{3}-\cancel{\frac{1}{4}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{4}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{5}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{5}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{7})].\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that for each partial sum, we always end up canceling all terms with the exception of the first and last terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=9[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{N+1}].
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{9}{n(n+1)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }9[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{N+1}] \\  & =9[\frac{1}{3}-0] \\  & =3\,.\end{aligned}
$$
